sections.skill: Calculate processing fees and include them in pricing

questions.prompt: Using 2.9 percent + 0.30 dollars, what is the fee on a 100-dollar sale?
questions.intro: When customers pay by card or app, the payment processor keeps a fee. A common structure is a percentage of the sale plus a fixed amount per transaction, for example (an assumption, not a real quote) 2.9 percent + 0.30 dollars. On a 40-dollar sale that is 0.029 x 40 + 0.30 = 1.46 dollars, so the business receives 38.54 dollars. The fixed part hurts small sales most: on a 3-dollar sale, 0.30 dollars alone is 10 percent. Include fees in cost per sale when setting prices.

sections.skill: Percent of an amount plus a fixed amount

questions.intro: Many fees follow "rate x amount + fixed." Change the percent to a decimal, multiply by the amount, then add the fixed part. Example: 3 percent of 50 plus 0.25: 0.03 x 50 = 1.50, then 1.50 + 0.25 = 1.75. A common mistake is forgetting the fixed part or using 3 instead of 0.03. Check: the fee should be much smaller than the sale.
